verdicts.summary: The combined rev-parse result is accepted only when exit code and line count agree exactly. Every mismatch I tried falls back to the old separate commands.
verdicts.scenario: I tried four cases. (1) A repo path with a newline: unborn HEAD gives 4 or more lines where 3 are expected, and a committed HEAD gives 5 or more where 4 are expected, so the strict equality check always falls back. (2) Git older than 2.31 echoes `--path-format=absolute` as an extra output line. It then yields 5 lines (committed) or 4 lines (unborn, exit 1), neither of which matches 4 or 3, so it falls back. (3) Exit 128 outside a repo or on a transient failure gives headChecked=false, so the fallback runs `resolveGitCommonDir`, which has no allowNonZeroExit and reports the old operation label and exit code. HEAD is then re-checked by `hasHeadCommit`, which is the old behaviour. (4) `--git-common-dir` is now absolute where it used to be relative and resolved against realPath(cwd). `tempIndexPath` is built with `path.join`, which normalizes it, and `--git-path index` was already absolute, so only the common dir changed form.
